description: One LFO read out at four fixed phases a quarter turn apart, each with its own waveform and its own frequency multiplier.

params.text: Sets the peak voltage of every output, 0V to 5V; at the bottom all four outputs stay at 0V.
Sets the base frequency, from about 0.004Hz to 1024Hz on an exponential scale.
Sets that channel's frequency as one, two or three times the base frequency.
Chooses that channel's waveform: sine, triangle or square.

inputs.text: Replaces the AMP knob while a cable is here: 0V to 10V sets the peak voltage from 0V to 5V.
Replaces the FREQ knob while a cable is here: 0V to 10V covers the same span the knob does.

outputs.text: The base phase, marked 2π because a whole turn brings it back to where it started.
A quarter turn ahead of the base phase.
Half a turn ahead of the base phase.
Three quarters of a turn ahead of the base phase.

notes: The two CV inputs replace their knobs rather than adding to them. With a cable in either one, turning that knob does nothing.
The multiplier is applied to the phase after the quarter-turn offset is worked out, so a channel set to two or three times no longer holds the quarter-turn spacing against the others.

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
